key_insight: Time-series forecasting models follow scaling behavior: a single training recipe yields consistent forecast-quality improvements across model sizes from 4M to 2.5B parameters, embodied in the open-weight Toto 2.0 family.
problem_solved: Addresses whether foundation-scale modeling and a unified training recipe can improve and generalize time-series forecasting performance and robustness across domains and model sizes.
method: Design and apply a single, reproducible training recipe across a family of five open-weight models spanning 4M–2.5B parameters (Toto 2.0).
Evaluate at scale on diverse benchmarks — BOOM (observability), GIFT-Eval (general forecasting), and TIME (contamination-resistant) — to measure accuracy and robustness.
Demonstrate consistent, state-of-the-art improvements and release models/weights for community use.
impact: Shows that foundation-model scaling is effective for forecasting, enabling practitioners to choose models by compute/latency budget while benefiting from a unified training recipe and open weights for transfer, deployment, and robust forecasting.
visual_elements: Scaling curve: line chart of model size (log params) vs. benchmark accuracy to show monotonic improvements.
Benchmark leaderboard: grouped bar chart comparing Toto 2.0 variants against prior SOTA across BOOM, GIFT-Eval, and TIME.
Architecture + recipe infographic: compact flow diagram highlighting the single training recipe applied uniformly to 5 model sizes.
Use-case icons: small visuals for observability, general forecasting, and contamination/robustness to connect benchmarks to real-world scenarios.
paper_title: Toto 2.0: Time Series Forecasting Enters the Scaling Era
paper_authors: Emaad Khwaja, Chris Lettieri, Gerald Woo, Eden Belouadah, Marc Cenac
